paper.title: MurmurHash2, MurmurHash2A, MurmurHash64A and MurmurHash64B and their SMHasher verification values
paper.venue: SMHasher reference repository (public domain; there is no peer-reviewed paper)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithms in the author's published reference source; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: MurmurHash2 (32-bit) passes the author's SMHasher verification value 0x27864C1E
MurmurHash2A passes the author's SMHasher verification value 0x7FBD4396
MurmurHash64A passes the author's SMHasher verification value 0x1F0D3804
MurmurHash64B passes the author's SMHasher verification value 0xDD537C05

each verification value is computed with the SMHasher procedure (256 hashes of the keys {0}, {0,1}, ... of length 0..255 with seed 256-length, then one hash of the concatenated outputs with seed 0, first 4 bytes little-endian), so it exercises every tail length and the block loop of its variant

expected_values_source.what: the four verification values in the hash table of main.cpp, and the verification procedure in VerificationTest of KeysetTest.cpp; the algorithms are from MurmurHash2.cpp
expected_values_source.url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aappleby/smhasher/master/src/main.cpp (also KeysetTest.cpp, MurmurHash2.cpp and Hashes.h, which fixes how the 64-bit variants take a 32-bit seed, in the same directory)
expected_values_source.note: the values are data, copied as numbers; the repository's code was not copied

negative_control: built with M2_R=23 (shift of the 32-bit block mix 23 instead of 24), MurmurHash2, 2A and 64B print FAIL (for example 4c47374c instead of 27864c1e) and the program exits 1; 64A does not use that constant and still passes
not_checked: any statistical or avalanche quality claim made for MurmurHash2 (SMHasher's other tests)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about real hardware)
big-endian behaviour, unaligned reads, the aligned and incremental variants (MurmurHashAligned2, CMurmurHash2A), MurmurHashNeutral2 and MurmurHash1
64-bit seeds (the verification procedure uses 32-bit seeds, so the upper seed half of MurmurHash64B is always 0)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the four verification values the MurmurHash2 author publishes, each over 256 hashes (1024 hashes in all). It does not show any quality claim about the hash.
